🇲🇽🌱 <u>THEY CANCELLED A NEOLIBERAL MEGA-AIRPORT. 500 SPECIES CAME BACK.</u>

Sheinbaum marked the return of 500 species to Lake Texcoco — the wetland the old regime wanted to pave over for the NAIM airport. "All that water would have had to be pumped out, because we couldn't have a flooded airport," she said. AMLO cancelled the project and turned the site into a protected ecological park; the valley kept its natural water regulator, and the migratory birds their home.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>PEOPLE POSING AS US AGENTS TRIED TO PULL A MEXICAN GOVERNOR INTO THEIR ORBIT</u>

Leaked audios show Baja California governor Marina del Pilar Ávila in contact with people "who presented themselves as agents or intermediaries of US authorities." Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch dismissed the manufactured scandal: nothing shared in federal security meetings carries "a sensitivity that worries us" — and he cautioned that no one even knows who those supposed agents really were. Foreign hands fishing in Mexican security; the channels held.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>TRUMP SAYS T-MEC IS DEAD. THE US CONGRESS DIDN'T GET THE MEMO</u>

On his first visit to the Capitol, Mexico's ambassador Roberto Lazzeri met a bipartisan group of lawmakers and left with a message that contradicts the White House: "it was very encouraging to confirm the broad support expressed by congress members of both parties for the strategic value of the T-MEC." Trump announced the deal wouldn't be renewed — the legislators who actually vote on trade think otherwise.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>PANAMA'S PRESIDENT COMES TO MEXICO CITY — INTEGRATION, NOT WASHINGTON'S ORBIT</u>

President José Raúl Mulino met Sheinbaum at Palacio Nacional today, arriving with ministers for trade, agriculture and the Canal — and 23 Mexican companies looking to expand into Panama. On the agenda: Panama joining a Latin America and Caribbean aerospace cooperation pact. As Washington threatens the region, two sovereign states build their own trade, investment and science ties.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE 55,000 WORKERS WHO NEVER EXISTED</u>

When formal employment looked like it dropped by 55,000 in May, the anti-4T press ran "job losses" headlines. Then the IMSS explained what actually happened: it detected a fake company simulating labor relations and deleted the ghost payroll. "No 55,000 jobs were lost because it was a fraud; those jobs never existed," said IMSS official Eduardo Alcaraz Prous. Risk models, inspections and home visits caught a pension-fraud scheme — not a downturn.

🇲🇽💧 <u>THE CUTZAMALA IS BACK</u>

The system that supplies water to more than 5 million people in the Valley of Mexico has climbed to 71.46% capacity — 559 million cubic meters — up from just 56.44% a year ago, a 15-point jump. Valle de Bravo alone now sits at 79%. Conagua credits sustained rainfall and "responsible water management" for a recovery two summers in the making.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>COOPERATION, NOT SUBORDINATION</u>

Mexico's National Security Council approved sending a pilot linked to the Mayo Zambada kidnapping to the US — one of 92 profiles transferred north under Mexico's own national security law, on Mexico's decision. Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said those handed over "were still making alliances with other criminal groups, committing homicide, extortion," and had done "much more damage here in Mexico than anywhere else."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>THE PAN GOVERNOR WHO LET THE CIA OPERATE ON MEXICAN SOIL</u>

Morena national leader Ariadna Montiel says Chihuahua governor Maru Campos didn't just permit US agents on Mexican territory — "no solamente lo planeó sino lo ejecutó, lo compartió y estuvo de acuerdo" (she didn't just plan it, she executed it, shared it, and agreed to it). Campos herself confirmed in interviews that the agents were CIA, operating without any federal authorization. Citizens in Chihuahua are now gathering signatures for a juicio político.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX IS CLOSING THE IMPORT VALVE</u>

Fuel imports fell 23.3% in the first quarter of 2026 while domestic refining jumped 22.2% to 1.141 million barrels a day — the National Refining System's fifth straight quarter of growth, led by the new Olmeca refinery (+164,000 bpd) and Tula's coker plant. From January to May, diesel imports dropped 29.5% year on year and imported gasoline fell 15.3%.

🇲🇽📚 <u>MEXICO JUST MADE ITS UNIVERSAL SCHOOL SCHOLARSHIP ACTUALLY UNIVERSAL</u>

New rules published this week in Mexico's official gazette (DOF) scrap the "gradual rollout" of the Rita Cetina universal scholarship in primary school — from this fiscal year, children enter the program from day one, whatever grade they're in. The Benito Juárez and Jóvenes Escribiendo el Futuro scholarships were updated the same day, with future-teacher students at federal and state normal schools reclassified as priority for direct payment.
